Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them.
Even when everyone’s got the best intentions, organizations can trip up on their OKR journey. Sound familiar? Spotting those common pitfalls—and knowing how to dodge them—can really be the difference between hitting a wall and actually making OKRs work.
First up: Setting too many OKRs. It’s easy to want to chase every single goal, but here’s the problem—when you try to do everything, you end up watering down your focus. The fix? Stay disciplined. Choose only the objectives that truly matter, and don’t be afraid to cut what’s not essential.
Next, let’s talk about vague or unmeasurable key results. If your key results are fuzzy, it’s almost impossible to know if you’re making progress. Want to avoid this? Get specific. Use numbers, set deadlines, and make sure your criteria are crystal clear.
Another big trap is treating OKRs as a performance evaluation tool. If hitting your OKRs is tied directly to promotions or pay, people might start playing it safe—or even sandbagging their goals. Instead, think of OKRs as a tool for learning and growth, not just a scorecard.
And what happens if there’s a lack of leadership buy-in? If leaders aren’t setting bold goals themselves, sharing updates, or talking openly about what’s working—and what isn’t—the rest of the team probably won’t either. Leaders have to walk the talk.
Then there’s the mistake of neglecting regular check-ins. OKRs aren’t something you set and forget. Without regular reviews, those goals just fade into the background. Short, frequent check-ins keep everyone on track, and make it easy to adjust course before it’s too late.
So, how do you keep your team on the right path? Try using a simple checklist:
Are our objectives focused and inspiring? Are our key results specific and measurable? Do we review progress regularly and make adjustments when needed? Are we using OKRs as a learning tool, not just for evaluation? And, is leadership actively engaged and transparent?
By keeping these questions front and center, you’ll steer clear of the common mistakes—and really unlock what OKRs can do for your organization.
